content.value: Primary reading: Rozanski and Woods, Chapter 27. Supplemental: SEI ATAM quality tradeoff framing. This unit focuses on operational resilience and incident learning.
Resilience depends on operations as much as structure. Observability, alerting, runbooks, drills, ownership, safe deployment, rollback, and incident review all shape the system ability to recover.
Architectural learning should continue after incidents. A post-incident review can reveal missing assumptions, hidden dependencies, poor recovery paths, or decisions that need to be revisited.
Studio: write three post-incident architecture questions that would help improve system resilience rather than merely assign blame.

concepts.name: Observability
concepts.description: The ability to understand internal system state from outputs such as logs, metrics, traces, and events.

concepts.name: Incident review
concepts.description: A structured examination of an operational incident to learn causes, impacts, and improvement actions.

concepts.name: Resilience drill
concepts.description: A planned exercise that tests recovery processes, failure handling, and operational readiness.

concepts.name: Safe deployment
concepts.description: A release approach that limits blast radius and enables detection, rollback, or mitigation of problems.
